mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically lower than during the 60-day pre-increase period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns as market anticipates a potential rate pause.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.4% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: Over 10 such inflation spikes, less than 40% of predicted 20-day forward returns are positive (binomial test p < 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a strengthening labor market, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Across 20 such labor market events, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeding 5% for two months indicates strengthening business demand, which typically precedes equity market optimism and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 such demand spikes, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the pre-spike mean (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 2% while HOUST (housing starts) remains flat or rises suggests supply-side softness, which can lead to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates a potential recession.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% for two consecutive months and HOUST does not decline
failure_condition: Over 8 such supply contractions, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 12 months prior to the contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months in a labor market recovery phase, it signals labor market absorption, which tends to boost equity valuations and produce positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 15 such low-unemployment episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the 60-day mean during the three months prior to the trend (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual decline in both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS (reserves) for four consecutive months indicates aggressive monetary tightening, which typically reduces credit availability and is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS each decline by >0.25% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: In 12 such tightening episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30 days prior to the start of the decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of the sum of all candidate proxies (GDPC1+PAYEMS+CPIAUCSL+FEDFUNDS+UNRATE+HOUST+INDPRO+RSAFS) is above its 2020–2022 historical median, the S&P 500 exhibits a higher than average 20-day forward return over the next month.
failure_condition: Over 40 such high-activity windows, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly above the 2020–2022 baseline (p > 0.05).
